=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27651-27779 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The new autofix-cap shadow-binding fallback (27708-27719) can bind the label to an older trusted latch, but the later-re-assertion guard (27651-27658), the revalidation (27737-27742) and the post-delete check (27774-27779) only look after the newest latch (`.key > $i` / `hl_latch_at`); a trusted comment that re-asserts `ai:needs-human` between the older bound latch and the newer unlabelled autofix-cap comment is never checked.
  WHY: Order: round-cap latch on head A, then an OWNER comment "keep `ai:needs-human`", then an unlabelled autofix-cap comment on head B, with the PR on head C; the fallback binds to the A latch and the poller deletes the label. This is a regression of the #9862 "no later re-assertion" condition and of the issue's non-goal "Auto-removing `ai:needs-human` set by a person". All five reviewers rated it MAJOR (mapped to high).
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27708-27719 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The fallback `any(.[]; .idx < $i and ... .head != $cur and (.login // "") == $e.login ...)` accepts any older stale-head candidate. It never checks whether a candidate between that one and the newest autofix-cap comment is a latch on the PR's current head.
  WHY: Order: stale latch on head A that the label binds to, then a latch on current head C (its label add is a no-op, or it is by the same login within 30 minutes), then an unlabelled autofix-cap comment; `any` short-circuits on the A candidate and the label is removed while a current-head hold is in force. Before this PR the case was skipped with `head_unchanged`, and the issue's non-goal is "Releasing a latch on the same head". All three rated it MAJOR (mapped to high); confidence ranged 3-4.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:4067-4070 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `review-round-infra-failed` marker artifact has `retention-days: 3`, but `SWEEP_REVIEW_ROUND_WINDOW_HOURS` / `cap_window_hours` accepts up to 9999 hours (scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:201-203).
  WHY: With a window over 72 hours, an infra-failed run's marker expires while the run is still inside the count window. The run then counts toward the cap, can escalate the PR to `ai:needs-human`, and no warning is logged. The default 48-hour window is unaffected. Severity disagreement: gemini and glm rated it MAJOR, minimax rated it NIT; the highest is used (high).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:release_head_bound_needs_human_latches, lines 27651-27658 (the re-assertion check is `any(to_entries[]; .key > $i ...)` with `--argjson i "${hl_latch_idx}"`), the new shadow-binding fallback at lines 27708-27719 (`any(.[]; .idx < $i ... .login == $e.login ...)`), and the revalidation and post-delete checks at lines 27737-27742 and 27774-27779 (`(.created_at // "") > $at` with `$at = hl_latch_at`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fallback binds the label to an older trusted latch, but every later-re-assertion guard still starts from the newest latch (the unlabelled autofix-cap comment), so a trusted re-assertion between the two latches is never checked; `hl_latch_candidates` holds only latch-marker comments, so a plain human comment is not in it either.
  WHY: Round-cap latch on head A, then OWNER "Keep `ai:needs-human` here", then an unlabelled autofix-cap comment with head marker B, with the PR on head C: the fallback binds to the round-cap comment, the label is deleted at line 27757, and a release is posted. This regresses #9862 "no later re-assertion" and the non-goal "Auto-removing `ai:needs-human` set by a person". Fix: return the matched candidate's idx and created_at from the fallback and re-run the line 27651 predicate and the revalidation and post-delete scans from them.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 27711-27716, `any(.[]; .idx < $i and ((.head // "") | test("^[0-9a-f]{40}$")) and .head != $cur and (.login // "") == $e.login ...)` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fallback never checks whether a candidate between the matched older one and the newest autofix-cap comment is a latch on the PR's current head.
  WHY: Round-cap latch on A (labelled at t+1m), then a latch on current head C at t+5m whose label add is a no-op, then an unlabelled autofix-cap comment: the newest label event binds to the A latch and the label is removed. This was previously skipped with `head_unchanged`. Fix: require that no candidate with idx < $i has `.head == $cur`.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "no release after a later human comment re-asserts the hold" (Tests section of issue #9917), together with the unchanged #9862 condition "no later re-assertion".
  Expected change site: tests/test_needs_human_head_latch_release.py, test_an_unlabelled_autofix_cap_comment_does_not_shadow_an_older_bound_latch (or a sibling test)
  Evidence of absence: test_a_later_comment_reasserting_the_hold_keeps_the_autofix_cap_label only places the re-asserting comment after the newest latch; no test covers a re-assertion between an older bound latch and a newer unlabelled autofix-cap comment.
  SEVERITY: NIT | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- HARDENING (2 related items, HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3):
  - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh lines 27708-27719: capture the bound candidate, re-apply the line 27651 predicate from its idx, and reject when an intermediate candidate has `.head == $cur` (~8 lines).
  - .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml / scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh lines 254-268: `retention-days: 3` against a window of up to 9999 hours (review_autofix_sweep.yml:661, review_sweep_round_cap.sh:203); `expired` is projected but never used. Document the 72-hour limit or derive retention from the window (~2 lines).

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27651-27658 and 27738-27745 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The re-assertion check for `ai:needs-human` latch release only scans comments after the newest latch candidate, so it ignores comments posted between an older selected latch and the newest one.
  WHY: An owner comment that re-asserts the hold between an older bound latch and a newer autofix-cap comment is ignored, and the label is removed despite it.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:4067-4070 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The infra-failure marker artifact is kept for 3 days, but the sweep round window can be set up to 9999 hours.
  WHY: With a window over 72 hours, infra-failed run artifacts expire while still inside the count window, so those rounds count toward the autofix budget and can park PRs incorrectly.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27708-27719 (the `any(.[]; .idx < $i; ...)` fallback block introduced by the LAST RUN DIFF), interacting with the later-re-assertion guard at 27651-27658, the revalidation at 27737-27744, and the post-delete check at 27774-27779 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fallback accepts binding via any older stale-head candidate without re-checking two kinds of intermediate event: (a) a trusted re-assertion between the older bound latch and the newest latch, which all three guards miss because they use `hl_latch_at` / `hl_latch_idx`; and (b) an intermediate latch candidate whose head equals the PR's current head.
  WHY: (a) Round-cap at idx=5 on A, OWNER "keep" at idx=10, unlabelled autofix-cap at idx=15 on B, PR on C: the fallback accepts via idx=5 and removes the label, contrary to the non-goal. (b) An intermediate round-cap at idx=10 on head C by OWNER within 30 minutes binds the label to the current head, but `any(...)` accepts via idx=5 anyway. The new test covers neither case.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:4070 (`retention-days: 3` on the `review-round-infra-failed` artifact), interacting with scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:201-203 (window-hours input validation accepts up to 9999) and :254-268 (artifacts listing keyed by `created_at`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The 72-hour marker retention is shorter than allowed windows (regex `^[1-9][0-9]{0,3}$`), and the README sets no upper bound.
  WHY: With a 96-hour window, markers older than 72 hours expire, the runs return to the count, and the PR can be escalated with `outcome=escalated`. An expired marker produces no warning, unlike the `infra_marker_read_failed` path.
- HARDENING (3 related items):
  - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh 27708-27719: return the matched candidate's `idx`, then re-run `later_needs_human_comment` over `(.key > $bound_idx and .key < $i)` and the time/login rule over the intermediate range (~12 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 5
  - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh 27608-27619: the run-based head fallback for autofix-cap comments with no marker; the existing `head_sha` 40-hex filter at line 27635 is sufficient, so no fix is needed. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 0
  - scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh 263-268: markers with a malformed or absent `created_at` are dropped silently; emit `REVIEW_SWEEP_ROUND_CAP outcome=infra_marker_malformed count=<n>` (~3 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
